video_title: Washington Wants The Market Even Lower | Weekly Roundup
gist: Jim and ex-market maker Nol argue the administration's post-midterm incentive is to let the market fall (while cutting the extreme left tail, as with the Nvidia/Jensen reversal), forecasting a stair-step decline into December opex and a 20-30% further S&P drop to 5,500-5,900 by June 2027, a Q1 Fed U-turn into money printing, and a gold-calls/sell-oil-puts trade. They stress that record index vol compression and dispersion mean calm-VIX grinding declines (2016, Q4 2018, 2022) tend to be the deepest.

insights.claim: Jim forecasts a 25-40% equity decline beginning after the midterms (likely starting before February) and completing between March and June 2027.
insights.speaker: Jim (guest, macro/flows strategist)
insights.so_what: Frames a defined window for downside hedges and re-entry; size and timing are explicit enough to track.
insights.quote: I've called for a 25 to 40% decline for sometime a you know starting sometime after the midterm likely before February would it would start um and be done sometime uh between March and June

insights.claim: Jim uses a 'three-legged stool' framework: macro, flows, and the incentives of a highly proactive administration, which he now treats as a market driver equal to the other two.
insights.speaker: Jim (guest, macro/flows strategist)
insights.so_what: Investors modeling only macro and positioning risk missing policy-driven path changes; add an explicit 'administration incentive' read.
insights.quote: if you're not playing that guy at the other side of the table, good luck, right?

insights.claim: Jim argues that after the midterms the administration's incentive shifted from supporting markets to allowing (or nudging) a decline, because large-scale QE requires a crisis to preserve the appearance of Fed independence under Worsh.
insights.speaker: Jim (guest, macro/flows strategist)
insights.so_what: Do not assume a policy put near current levels; the put sits lower, after a crisis justifies QE.
insights.quote: Show me the incentives. I'll show you the outcome.

insights.claim: Jim reads the weekend Nvidia/Jensen reversal (Bessent changing tune) as the administration 'selling puts' to cut the left tail, while still wanting the market lower — a put exists, but it is deep out of the money.
insights.speaker: Jim (guest, macro/flows strategist)
insights.so_what: Favors selling-side trades (short delta with vol compression) while avoiding bets on a disorderly crash.
insights.quote: the administration just told you they're not willing to deal with a big fat tail and lose control, but they still want the market to go lower. That is a huge signal.

insights.claim: Jim's most likely path is a stair-step decline into December opex, with an alternative path of a short 'ripper' rally plus vol compression before rolling over; he structures roughly delta-neutral to slightly short delta to profit from either.
insights.speaker: Jim (guest, macro/flows strategist)
insights.so_what: Path-specific options structures can monetize both scenarios; outright directional bets are less efficient.
insights.quote: stairst steps till December are overwhelmingly likely

insights.claim: Jim's 2027 path targets: S&P 500 visits 5,500-5,900 by June 2027 then bounces; NASDAQ has a deeper cut and deeper bounce; overall another 20-30% decline from current levels.
insights.speaker: Jim (guest, macro/flows strategist)
insights.so_what: Concrete levels for put strikes and re-entry planning; Nasdaq is the higher-beta expression of the short.

insights.claim: Jim warns China appears to have intervened meaningfully and would like a deeper, less-recoverable market decline, making the administration's controlled-decline plan less certain.
insights.speaker: Jim (guest, macro/flows strategist)
insights.so_what: Adds fatter left tail risk than the base case; keep some convex downside protection.
insights.quote: There are other players sitting at that poker table and China's sitting over there playing a hand.

insights.claim: Jim argues the macro economy has been rolling over for most sectors but was levitated by a narrow AI trade whose earnings growth is largely a capex story tied to the equity market itself.
insights.speaker: Jim (guest, macro/flows strategist)
insights.so_what: AI-linked earnings are reflexive to equity prices; a market decline can hit reported growth, not just multiples.

insights.claim: Jim says hyperscalers no longer have cash on their books after committing huge capex (e.g. $400-600B pledges at a September Trump meeting, including a Zuckerberg 'was the 600 billion too much?' hot-mic moment), so further buildout depends on debt markets.
insights.speaker: Jim (guest, macro/flows strategist)
insights.so_what: Watch hyperscaler debt issuance and funding costs as the gating factor for AI capex continuation.
insights.quote: there's no longer any cash on hyperscaler books

insights.claim: Jim says credit default swaps started blowing out in October when the 10-year yield hit about 5.3-5.4%, as AI capex debt began crowding out sovereign debt.
insights.speaker: Jim (guest, macro/flows strategist)
insights.so_what: CDS spreads on AI-capex issuers are a leading indicator for the equity rollover thesis.

insights.claim: Jim flags the five-year anniversary of the 2021 zero-rate refinancing boom: 5-7 year debt rolling over now pressures the long end alongside AI capex funding needs, leaving 'not enough money to go around' absent a Fed/Treasury buyer of last resort.
insights.speaker: Jim (guest, macro/flows strategist)
insights.so_what: Supports expectations of eventual Fed/Treasury balance-sheet support and long-end supply pressure.
insights.quote: there's just not enough money to go around. Unless, this is the big unless the investor of last resort, the buyer of last resort steps in.

insights.claim: Jim believes the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen for another one to three years or possibly ever, implying structurally higher costs that weigh on the economy.
insights.speaker: Jim (guest, macro/flows strategist)
insights.so_what: Supports a structural energy-cost premium and stagflationary pressure on demand.

insights.claim: Jim says Fed hawkishness, including Waller's call for a 50bp hike, is 'Kabuki theater' for credibility so the US does not look like a banana republic, while Trump, Bessent and Worsh ultimately want to print.
insights.speaker: Jim (guest, macro/flows strategist)
insights.so_what: Fade the priced hiking path; position for a fast U-turn to easing and money printing.
insights.quote: They all want to print print print and we are going to print print and it's going to happen in the next seven, eight months.

insights.claim: Jim expects a Fed U-turn around Q1 2027 followed by heavy money printing, and endorses selling the front end then moving to a curve steepener; he says he is betting real money on it.
insights.speaker: Jim (guest, macro/flows strategist)
insights.so_what: Trade: front-end receivers/SOFR longs into the pivot, then steepeners once printing begins.

insights.claim: Host notes markets still price two to three-plus more rate hikes, with front-end vol whipsawing (two hikes in, one out, half back in within weeks) while long-dated Treasury vol stays benign.
insights.speaker: Quinn (host)
insights.so_what: Front-end rates volatility is where the mispricing and opportunity sit versus a calm long end.

insights.claim: Jim says the long end is caught between macro demand rollover and structural inflation plus debt refinancing; the fact it is holding up despite inelastic inflation signals a pretty bad macro rollover.
insights.speaker: Jim (guest, macro/flows strategist)
insights.so_what: Expect long-end vol to stay lower than front-end vol; refinancing waves cap rallies in long bonds.

insights.claim: Jim's 10-year path: visits about 3.8-3.9% (barely undercutting), then rises back to 5.5-6%, possibly capped near 5.5% by official buying.
insights.speaker: Jim (guest, macro/flows strategist)
insights.so_what: A round-trip in long yields argues for tactical duration then a curve steepener/short duration later.

insights.claim: Host flags a tail risk of a Liberation Day-style 'everything down' move — dollar, bonds and equities falling together — after strong flows into US assets and a strong dollar.
insights.speaker: Quinn (host)
insights.so_what: Conventional bond hedges may fail; gold is the asset cited as working in that regime.

insights.claim: Jim reissues his late-2021 trade: buy gold calls and sell oil puts premium-neutral about a year out, saying another gold run comes within 6-9 months.
insights.speaker: Jim (guest, macro/flows strategist)
insights.so_what: Explicit, repeatable cross-asset options structure with defined horizon.
insights.quote: You're going to get another run in gold gold calls uh sell oil puts. That's the trade.

insights.claim: Jim cites 1968-1982 as the analog: gold was the best-performing asset and best vol to own, equity vol and industrial commodity vol were massive sales as equities went nowhere for 14 years in nominal terms, and oil vol compressed despite structural inflation.
insights.speaker: Jim (guest, macro/flows strategist)
insights.so_what: In a Nixon-like stagflationary regime, own gold convexity and sell equity/commodity vol.

insights.claim: Jim compares Trump to Nixon and says the current setup feels like Nixon's post-midterm period.
insights.speaker: Jim (guest, macro/flows strategist)
insights.so_what: Points investors to the early-1970s playbook for policy-pressured markets.

insights.claim: Jim expects gold to dip slightly further then rise about 20% by June 2027 at the start of a big cycle run; he likes that people have lost faith in gold.
insights.speaker: Jim (guest, macro/flows strategist)
insights.so_what: Use gold calls (not just delta) to capture the expected breakout with defined risk.

insights.claim: Jim expects WTI to fall to the low 60s or even 50s on demand weakness, then re-accelerate sharply because supply has become inelastic, with a possible 55-140 range — downside linear, upside explosive.
insights.speaker: Jim (guest, macro/flows strategist)
insights.so_what: Asymmetric oil skew: sell downside vol, own upside convexity after the demand-driven drop.

insights.claim: Host notes every commodity is down since the Fed hiked in September, copper is making new lows, and futures-positioning deleveraging is the largest in some time — a prolonged growth scare is the regime people are least prepared for.
insights.speaker: Quinn (host)
insights.so_what: Max-pain scenario is a hawkish-Fed growth scare without quick rescue; cyclical commodities stay pressured.

insights.claim: Jim says index-level vol compression from structured product issuance and multi-year LEAPS is the largest ever into this December opex, the biggest options expiration ever, creating supportive dealer flows that bounce every selloff.
insights.speaker: Jim (guest, macro/flows strategist)
insights.so_what: Expect supported, grinding price action into opex; crash bets before then fight the flow.
insights.quote: This December opex is the biggest options expiration ever.

insights.claim: Jim argues realized dispersion since 2017 has no precedent in 80-100 years of data, and the correlation breakdown is structurally driven by options/structured-product flows, not macro.
insights.speaker: Jim (guest, macro/flows strategist)
insights.so_what: Index vol is structurally suppressed; dispersion trades persist until vol supply dries up.

insights.claim: Jim says a 40 VIX for a day is not enough to break the regime; it needs higher back-end vega, vol supply going away, lighter structured product issuance and real pain, which has not happened.
insights.speaker: Jim (guest, macro/flows strategist)
insights.so_what: Watch long-dated vega and structured-product issuance as the real regime-change signals, not spot VIX.

insights.claim: Nol notes implied correlation came from all-time lows and rises nonlinearly: from 10 to 20 to 30 then jumps 30 to 60 to 80-90 as forced unwinds (e.g. a multi-pod firm short $500M vega) create liquidity vacuums.
insights.speaker: Nol (guest, ex-market maker, QVR co-founder)
insights.so_what: Cheap correlation/index convexity can pay off disproportionately once forced deleveraging starts.

insights.claim: Nol says post-GFC you could sell 10-year OTC variance swaps at 30, yet back-end vol has barely moved now despite a 40 VIX, underscoring how little long-dated vol has repriced.
insights.speaker: Nol (guest, ex-market maker, QVR co-founder)
insights.so_what: Back-end vol looks underpriced relative to the macro risk; potential long-dated vol buying opportunity.
insights.quote: 40 VIX for a day. Nothing. Absolutely nothing.

insights.claim: Jim argues 'market structure is supply and demand' and the most reliable predictor of outcomes, since macro can only reach prices through supply and demand.
insights.speaker: Jim (guest, macro/flows strategist)
insights.so_what: Prioritize positioning and flow data over macro narratives for timing.

insights.claim: Jim says options are the underlying distribution of every asset class and 'vol is not an asset class'; investors should think distributionally rather than up/down.
insights.speaker: Jim (guest, macro/flows strategist)
insights.so_what: Use options to express path and time views, not just direction.
insights.quote: V is not an asset class. If you say V is an asset class, you got it all wrong.

insights.claim: Jim's historical pattern: deeper, more painful declines happen when vol does not explode because everyone is hedged — 2016 (13%) after the 2015 yuan shock (9%), Q4 2018 (about 19-20% in three months) after Volmageddon (9%), and 2022 (about 27% over nine months).
insights.speaker: Jim (guest, macro/flows strategist)
insights.so_what: A grinding decline with calm VIX is a warning, not reassurance; long stock plus long puts can underperform.
insights.quote: usually you get deeper worse cuts when vault doesn't explode

insights.claim: Jim says because many investors are now hedged with puts rather than selling stock, the coming pain is more likely a 2022-style grind than a Q4 2018 V-bottom.
insights.speaker: Jim (guest, macro/flows strategist)
insights.so_what: Puts may decay in a slow decline; consider short-delta and put-spread structures over outright long puts.

insights.claim: Nol says the best 2022 trade was effectively inverse buy-writes (short the market, short puts), contrasting with COVID when puts worked; investors fight the last battle.
insights.speaker: Nol (guest, ex-market maker, QVR co-founder)
insights.so_what: In a grinding bear, collecting premium while short delta can beat owning puts.

insights.claim: Host notes NASDAQ had two 5% down days in three weeks that felt methodical rather than panicky, frustrating investors because there was no clearing event.
insights.speaker: Quinn (host)
insights.so_what: Lack of capitulation signals the decline is not finished.

insights.claim: Host observes the Monday equity bounce was not confirmed: rates priced a more hawkish path, credit lagged, long-end yields fell, and copper kept making new lows — a growth-scare, disinflationary bust signal.
insights.speaker: Quinn (host)
insights.so_what: Use cross-asset confirmation (credit, long yields, copper) to judge whether equity rallies are durable.

insights.claim: Nol clarifies his call was buying VIX put spreads/ratios on a risk-defined small book allocation, betting vol fades from 40 over 40-50 days into the holidays — not a buy-the-dip call.
insights.speaker: Nol (guest, ex-market maker, QVR co-founder)
insights.so_what: Short-vol via defined-risk VIX puts can coexist with a bearish equity view.
insights.quote: I said I would buy ratios or put spreads in VIX. That's not the same thing as buying the dip.

insights.claim: Nol says the market can always be rescued by government action, which may be inflationary over time, because there is broad appetite for risk assets at lower levels.
insights.speaker: Nol (guest, ex-market maker, QVR co-founder)
insights.so_what: Supports eventual buying of a deep drawdown and inflation hedges for the rescue aftermath.

insights.claim: Nol says there is no single signal for stair-step vs correlation-to-one crashes; he assesses positioning, gamma that disappears as puts go deep in the money, and cross-asset vol across ES, SPX, UPRO, VIX and QQQ to gauge counterparties' pain points.
insights.speaker: Nol (guest, ex-market maker, QVR co-founder)
insights.so_what: Monitor where large short-put positions hit max pain across related instruments, not a single VIX threshold.

insights.claim: Nol emphasizes time as an edge: selling high vol and collecting theta can make money even if markets go nowhere.
insights.speaker: Nol (guest, ex-market maker, QVR co-founder)
insights.so_what: In elevated-vol regimes, theta harvesting is a non-directional return source.
